items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: James Whitcomb Riley was a homespun Midwestern poet. He was hip. He knew a lot.

ctx.x: So you’re recording people on the air, you’re interviewing, and then eventually the live things from the remote. You mentioned at this time – it’s just fascinating to think about your – you were the announcer for Curley, for the mayor. Could you give us a sketch of political corruption in Boston?

Curley was bigger than that. If you want to see James Michael Curley – if you’re lucky, you might see on late night television The Last Hurrah with Spencer Tracy. That is about as accurate as you can get the personification of Curley. Curley was – first of all, he had a voice like an organ. He had studied diction and speaking at Emerson College, but he was also a natural orator with a very keen sense of his audiences. He also didn’t use any notes when he did these radio broadcasts. Once I did have to cut him off…
What’s Riley? I don’t understand that.
